title: The three AIF categories
objectives: Name the three AIF categories, what each invests in, and their structure.
Say which category can use leverage.
body_md:
Category I: early-stage and socially or economically desirable sectors. Closed-ended, minimum 3-year tenure. Examples: venture capital, SME, social impact, infrastructure, angel funds. Category II: everything not in Cat I or III; no leverage except for temporary needs. Closed-ended, minimum 3-year tenure. Examples: private equity, private credit, real estate funds. Category III: complex or trading strategies, may use leverage within limits. Open-ended or closed-ended. Examples: long-short equity, hedge-style funds.

| Category | What it invests in | Structure | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category I | Early-stage and socially or economically desirable sectors | Closed-ended, minimum 3-year tenure | Venture capital, SME, social impact, infrastructure, angel funds |
| Category II | Everything not in Cat I or III; no leverage except for temporary needs | Closed-ended, minimum 3-year tenure | Private equity, private credit, real estate funds |
| Category III | Complex or trading strategies, may use leverage within limits | Open-ended or closed-ended | Long-short equity, hedge-style funds |
example: Venture capital fund → Category I. Private credit fund → Category II. Long-short equity fund → Category III.
say: Category I and II are closed-ended, minimum 3-year tenure.
Only Category III may use leverage within limits.

check.q: Which AIF category includes venture capital and angel funds?
check.why: Category I. Cat I covers early-stage and socially or economically desirable sectors.

check.q: Which AIF category includes private equity and private credit funds?
check.why: Category II. Cat II covers private-market funds.

check.q: Which AIF category may use leverage and run long-short strategies?
check.why: Category III. Cat III runs complex or trading strategies.
